Roadmap.title: Your personal roadmap
Roadmap.intro: Answer a few questions and get a personal to-do list with dates. Your answers are stored only in this browser and are not sent to a server.
Roadmap.permit: Which permit are you coming with?
Roadmap.household: Who is coming with you, or will join you?
Roadmap.confirmReset: Delete the roadmap and your ticks?
Roadmap.note: This list is general information and does not assess your personal situation. Always check deadlines and requirements with the competent authority. The dates are a suggestion based on your arrival date.

documents.title: Prepare documents: Turkish records, apostille, sworn translation
documents.note: Multilingual extracts need no apostille; ask the authority about the translation.

diploma.title: Check the recognition of your degree (anabin)
diploma.note: If needed, apply for a ZAB assessment or professional recognition; it takes about 3 months.

languageVisa.title: Prepare your German certificate for the visa
languageVisa.note: Usually A1 for family reunion, B1 for Ausbildung; ask which certificate is accepted.

visa.title: Apply for the visa
visa.note: Book the appointment early; check the document list with the German mission.

blockedAccount.title: Open a blocked account (Sperrkonto)
blockedAccount.note: Proof of funds for the Opportunity Card; confirm the amount with the mission.

housing.title: Find a flat and get the lease and the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung
housing.note: You need the landlord's confirmation for the Anmeldung.

healthChoose.title: Choose your health insurer
healthChoose.note: Apply for membership before you start work and tell your employer.

anmeldung.title: Anmeldung: register your address
anmeldung.note: Legal deadline: two weeks after moving in; do it in the first week.

deutschlandticket.title: Transport: set up the Deutschlandticket
deutschlandticket.note: Cancellable monthly; cancelling by the 10th ends it at month end.

residencePermit.title: Book an appointment at the Ausländerbehörde for your residence permit
residencePermit.note: If you entered with a visa, start before the visa expires.

bank.title: Open a bank account
bank.note: You need the registration certificate; accepted documents differ by bank.

schufa.title: Get a SCHUFA BonitätsAuskunft for flat applications
schufa.note: The free data copy is not suitable for landlords.

taxId.title: Check for the tax ID letter and give it to your employer
taxId.note: It arrives by post after the Anmeldung.

taxClass.title: Choose your tax class together (if married)
taxClass.note: III/V or IV with Faktorverfahren; ask the Finanzamt.

rundfunkbeitrag.title: Register for the Rundfunkbeitrag
rundfunkbeitrag.note: One fee per dwelling; do not register twice with your flatmates.

doctor.title: Find a Hausarzt and learn the difference between 112 and 116117
doctor.note: Specialists may need a referral and an urgency code.

familyInsurance.title: Apply for family insurance
familyInsurance.note: The family member must live in Germany; check the income limit.

kindergeld.title: Apply for Kindergeld
kindergeld.note: Tax ID and the type of residence permit matter; the Opportunity Card gives no entitlement.

kita.title: Apply for a Kita voucher and a Kita place
kita.note: Rules differ by city; ask the Jugendamt.

integrationCourse.title: Check your entitlement to an integration course
integrationCourse.note: The entitlement expires one year after the permit is issued; request the fee exemption before the course starts.

bzst.title: Contact the BZSt if the tax ID has not arrived
bzst.note: Three months after the Anmeldung, with ID and registration confirmation.

driving.title: Start exchanging your Turkish driving licence
driving.note: 6 months from taking residence; a test is required for Turkey.

languageB1.title: Get a German B1 certificate
languageB1.note: Required for permanent residence and naturalisation.

permBlueCard.title: Apply for permanent residence with the Blue Card
permBlueCard.note: 21 months with B1, 27 months with A1; pension contributions and qualified work required.

permSkilled.title: Apply for permanent residence (skilled worker)
permSkilled.note: 3 years and 36 months of pension contributions; sufficient German.

permStandard.title: Apply for permanent residence (standard route)
permStandard.note: 5 years and 60 months of pension contributions; check the requirements.

citizenship.title: Apply for naturalisation (Einbürgerung)
citizenship.note: 5 years, B1, the Einbürgerungstest and secured livelihood.

Lid.title: Life in Germany test: official practice
Lid.intro: The Leben in Deutschland test and the Einbürgerungstest draw on the same pool of questions. The best preparation is the BAMF's official question catalogue. We do not copy the questions here; we point you to the official source.

center.title: BAMF Online-Testcenter
center.text: Practise the catalogue interactively; the right answer is shown after each question. Includes a sample test.

catalog.title: Gesamtfragenkatalog (PDF)
catalog.text: The official list of all questions: 300 nationwide questions plus state-specific ones.

course.title: Integration course and final test (BAMF)
course.text: Official information about the final examination and the certificate.

facts: 33 questions: 30 for all of Germany, 3 for your state
Orientation course test: at least 15 correct
The catalogue has 310 questions (300 nationwide, 10 per state)
tips: Start with the sample test and see where you have gaps.
Study your own state's questions separately: 3 questions in the test are state questions.
Note the questions you got wrong and retry them after a few days.
For registration and fees see our guide.
Lid.note: This page is not an official service. The links lead to BAMF websites; always download the current question catalogue from the BAMF.

About.title: About
About.intro: Pusula is a guide for newcomers and people living in Germany, Turkish first (also German and English). Its aim: explain official matters clearly, with sources and dates.
About.p1: For people planning a move to Germany, new arrivals, and anyone finding their way through paperwork in the first years. The information is general and is not a binding answer for your situation.
About.h2: How do we write and check a guide?
verify: We take information from official sources first: statute text, ministries, the BAMF, the Federal Employment Agency, the Federal Foreign Office, the responsible authority's own page.
Every guide shows its sources and the date of the last check.
A guide without sources and a verification date is not published. Facts we cannot verify are left out.
Figures that change often, such as fees, thresholds and deadlines, are managed in one place and updated in all guides at once.
A guide last checked more than 90 days ago shows a "check again" notice.
German and English translations are marked "review pending" until a native speaker has read them.
About.p3: "Experience" posts on the blog are personal stories. They are not rules; dates and conditions change. They are kept apart from the guides.
About.p4: The site does not earn money at the moment. If advertising or affiliate links are added later, they will be clearly marked "Ad" and will not influence the content or the order.
About.p5: The roadmap and theme setting are stored in your browser only. We use no analytics or advertising cookies. Details are in the privacy policy.
About.correctionsText: If you see wrong or outdated information, please write to us; we will correct it with a source.

Letters.title: Templates for cancellations and objections
Letters.intro: Fill in the fields, then copy or print the German letter. What you enter stays in your browser and is sent nowhere.
Letters.rentalIntro: Create a German cover letter for a rental application. You can copy it or print it.
Letters.disclaimer: These templates are general examples, not legal advice. Have someone who reads German check important letters (cancellation, objection, flat application) before you send them.
Letters.pendingFill: The letter appears here once the required fields are filled in.

templates.cancelContract: Cancel a contract (phone, internet, gym, energy…)

notes.rentalApplication: The letter is created in German. Send landlords only the documents they need; do not attach sensitive documents such as an ID copy or bank statements with the first application.
notes.cancelContract: Check the notice period and form in your contract. For proof, consider registered mail or documenting how you sent it.
notes.cancelLease: Terminating a residential lease must be in writing with your own signature (§ 568 BGB). The notice period for tenants is usually three months (§ 573c BGB); check your contract. An email is not enough.
notes.objection: The deadline to object is usually one month after you receive the decision; the exact deadline is in the notice's legal remedy instructions (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung). Do not miss it. In important cases get advice or a lawyer.
notes.appointment: Also check whether the authority books appointments online; many immigration offices only do so online.

Insurance.title: Which insurance do I need?
Insurance.intro: A few questions show which insurance is mandatory, strongly recommended or worth considering for you. Your answers stay in your browser.

q.hasFamily: Do a partner or children live in your household?
q.ownsValuables: Do you own things you could not easily replace (furniture, electronics)?
q.travelsAbroad: Do you travel abroad (including to Turkey)?
q.relyOnIncome: Does your household depend on your work income?

health.title: Health insurance (Krankenversicherung)
health.text: Mandatory for everyone living in Germany: statutory (GKV) or private. For employees the employer usually pays a share.

care.title: Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung)
care.text: Tied to health insurance and mandatory; with statutory insurance it comes automatically.

liability.title: Personal liability insurance (Haftpflicht)
liability.text: Not required by law, but considered the most important voluntary insurance because damage to others can be very expensive. Many landlords ask for it.

carLiability.title: Car liability insurance (Kfz-Haftpflicht)
carLiability.text: Mandatory to use a vehicle on the road.

dogLiability.title: Dog liability insurance
dogLiability.text: Mandatory in some states and common in others; check your state's rule.

disability.title: Occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeit)
disability.text: Protects your income if illness or an accident stops you working. Terms and premiums vary a lot; compare.

household.title: Contents insurance (Hausrat)
household.text: Covers damage to your belongings from fire, water or burglary. Worth considering depending on their value.

legal.title: Legal expenses insurance (Rechtsschutz)
legal.text: Covers lawyer and court costs. There are usually waiting periods; you cannot take it out once a dispute has started.

travelHealth.title: Travel health insurance abroad
travelHealth.text: Statutory insurance may not cover everything abroad, especially outside the EU (including Turkey); travel health cover including repatriation is worth considering.

accident.title: Accident insurance (Unfallversicherung)
accident.text: Can add protection, especially for children and leisure accidents; coverage is limited, so check whether you need it.

Insurance.disclaimer: This result is general information, not insurance advice or a product recommendation. Compare terms and prices before you sign, and if needed get neutral information from a consumer centre (Verbraucherzentrale).

Holidays.title: Public holidays and bridge days
Holidays.intro: See the public holidays in the state where you work and find bridge days for long breaks with few days off.
Holidays.bridgesIntro: When a holiday falls on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday, a few days of leave give you a long break.
Holidays.noBridges: There are no bridge-day suggestions for this state and year.
Holidays.localNote: Days marked "only in some municipalities" are not a holiday across the whole state; check your municipality. They are not counted in the bridge days.
Holidays.disclaimer: The list is based on the states' holiday laws and the DGB overview, checked on {date}. The state where you work decides; your employment or collective agreement may differ. The holiday law of your state is binding. Dates are checked for 2026 and 2027 only.
